issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class defines a getter named retrieveQuantity(), but other parts of the template (Stock and Main) and the problem statement expect a conventional getter named getQuantity(). This name mismatch causes compilation errors and contradicts the problem instruction to "add getters for all the private fields." The solution repository uses getQuantity(), so students following the template will be confused when code referring to getQuantity() does not compile.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the method retrieveQuantity() in the template StockIngredient to getQuantity(), or update all callers to use retrieveQuantity(). Preferably implement getQuantity() (and keep retrieveQuantity if desired) so that the template, solution, and problem statement consistently provide/get the same getter name for quantity.

issues.description: The quantity getter for StockIngredient is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template defines retrieveQuantity(), while Stock.java in the template calls getQuantity(), and the solution uses getQuantity(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" (implying standard getter names). This mismatch creates a direct compilation/mapping problem and cognitive confusion about the expected getter name for quantity.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent standard getter name for the quantity field across all artifacts. Rename retrieveQuantity() in the template StockIngredient to getQuantity(), or alternatively update Stock.java to call retrieveQuantity(), but prefer using getQuantity() to match the solution and conventional getter naming.
